about: Open space for an IT team: what to plan

An open-space office works when there is somewhere to escape the general noise. So we plan not only rows of desks but also a quiet zone, phone booths, meeting rooms of different sizes and a place for informal discussions. Teams that work together sit together; those who need quiet sit away from the kitchen and entrance.
We plan for growth: spare workstations, network and power capacity, flexible zones that can be rearranged without a new renovation.
Acoustics: so the open space does not get loud

The main complaint about open offices is noise. It is solved as a system: acoustic panels on walls and ceilings, soft flooring, desk screens, phone booths and properly insulated meeting rooms. We put the solutions into the design from the start — reworking after the renovation costs more.

Office Chicago is a completed office in the Chicago residential complex in Kyiv: zoning without solid walls, green walls and an island of live plants between desks, linear lighting over workstations, a kitchen-café. The space is open, but every zone has its own function.

After the design — office renovation from $350/m² (works and rough materials) by our salaried team. faq: How much does open-space office design cost?
From $30 per m², minimum project fee $2,500. Office renovation from $350 per m² (works and rough materials); finishing materials, furniture and equipment separately, per estimate.
How do you make an open space quiet?
As a system: acoustic wall and ceiling panels, soft flooring, desk screens, phone booths and sound-insulated meeting rooms. We put all of this into the design before the renovation.
Does an open-space office need private rooms?
Usually yes: at least a few meeting rooms and a quiet zone. Most often we design a mixed layout — open seats plus closed rooms for calls and meetings.
Can I order only the design project?
Yes. But the risks are lowest when design, renovation and furniture are handled by one team.
